account:
Today I have followed my mayoral appointments: the morning market walk, lunch at home, and now the one-o'clock town accounts at the office. The builder has been waiting to agree this week's public repairs and payment, carrying a lantern and saying he has planks and lanterns ready. I requested specific damaged locations and an itemized proposal before authorizing anything. I have not yet heard a concrete repair report or agreed to work or payment. The secretary is nearby with a writable book and offered earlier to record an agreement. This appears to be ordinary town business, though the scope and budget remain unresolved.

Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, and later bread at the inn. I personally saw the baker put bread into the market-stall chest. Those movements could simply be baking, stocking the stall, and supplying the inn; I have no evidence of anything improper or unusual beyond the repeated reports. I heard distant conversations involving the baker and freight, including a shout from the baker, but could not understand them and do not know their purpose.

My three-o'clock appointment is tea with a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank. The appointment book does not identify the neighbour or house number, and the secretary did not know. My attempts to ask freight were out of hearing range, so that detail is still unresolved. I should not mistake those unheard exchanges for answers.
